title: ranunculus glacialis subsp. camissonis
intro: Ranunculus glacialis subsp. camissonis, commonly known as Camissonia or Island Plume Poppy, is a plant species within the Onagraceae family. This plant has been used in traditional medicine for its potential health benefits, which include reducing inflammation and alleviating respiratory issues, such as asthma and bronchitis. The therapeutic actions of Camissonia are attributed to its ability to relax the airways and reduce spasms, while its bioactive constituents, including flavonoids and phenolic acids, contribute to its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. However, the plant is highly toxic and should be handled with caution, as it contains the toxic compound ranunculin.
